title: Corneal Endothelial Changes After Phacoemulsification Using the Eight-Chop Technique in Diabetic Eyes

license.statement: CC BY 4.0 (article <license>: 'Creative Commons Attribution (CC BY) license', link https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)

indication: Age-related cataract (Emery nucleus grade II-III), 181 eyes of 138 patients; diabetes diagnosed from HbA1c within 6 months before surgery (cut-off not stated); diabetic retinopathy, corneal disease or opacity, uveitis, poor dilation (< 5.0 mm), white cataract, preoperative CECD < 2000 cells/mm2, severely weak zonules and previous ocular trauma or surgery excluded

groups.description: Diabetes group: phacoemulsification with the eight-chop technique (nucleus pre-divided into eight segments with an eight-chopper, Centurion system, 3.0 mm temporal clear corneal incision, sodium hyaluronate, in-the-bag Acrysof MN60AC IOL, intracameral moxifloxacin) by one surgeon experienced in the technique; 94 eyes, Sato Eye Clinic, June 2019 to July 2022
Control group (the authors' label): patients without diabetes operated with the same eight-chop technique, surgeon and system in the same period; 87 operated eyes

exclusions.what: jpm-15-00209-t003 CV and PHC rows; Tables 1, 2, 4 and 5 (operative parameters, CECD, IOP, BCVA)
Postoperative day 1 and 2, week 1 and week 3 visits (Methods 2.5)
exclusions.reason: No CCT reported for these visits

notes: Both groups underwent the same standard technique of this surgeon (eight-chop); diabetes defines a patient-condition subgroup, so both groups are control role. The authors' 'Control Group' is an operated nondiabetic group, not unoperated eyes.
181 eyes of 138 patients: some patients contributed both eyes, so eyes within a group are not all independent.
Table 3 caption reads 'endothelial CCT'; footnote and Methods define CCT as central corneal thickness measured with the specular microscope.
